answers.statement: The pilot tests the stated claim; an instance satisfying all assumptions with a different outcome refutes it.
Baseline: the open-loop policy class; environment: the finite family in the input plan; no data; CPU only.
Frozen: claim, family, policy class, working equivalence definition. Nothing required for the pilot is missing.
Continue if no counterexample; a counterexample abandons the claim. Finite support never proves the general statement.
Not a v3 task: a registered local theory pilot (exact computation).

payload.hypothesis: In the binary-action family with immediately observed rewards r_t = 1[a_t = theta_t], V*_B(history) equals V*_A(open-loop), so the gap V*_A(history) - V*_B(history) equals the value of using history in A
payload.falsification: an instance in the family with V*_B(history) != V*_A(open-loop)

environment.family: binary actions, rewards observed, H<=3, p in {1/2,1/3,2/3,1/4}

payload.theorem_statement: In the binary-action family with immediately observed rewards r_t = 1[a_t = theta_t], V*_B(history) equals V*_A(open-loop), so the gap V*_A(history) - V*_B(history) equals the value of using history in A
assumptions: same policy class in A and B
payload.policy_information_class: deterministic policies over own past actions and rewards (identical in A and B); randomised policies cannot do better
